complianceguardian-kcqs32.name: ComplianceGuardian
complianceguardian-kcqs32.summary: Every verdict cites the rule it came from. Upload a document, get a Gemini risk score in seconds - routine cases auto-approve, edge cases reach a human, audit trail immutable.

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: They built the thing that survives the no-budget, no-internet, no-permission case.
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: Every verdict cites the rule it came from. Upload a document, get a Gemini risk score in seconds - routine cases auto-approve, edge cases reach a human, audit trail immutable.
steal_this: Store the citation as a first-class row, not a footnote. The moment evidence is structured, 'explain yourself' becomes a SELECT.
Decide which single action is expensive enough to require a human, and make that gate a schema state transition rather than a prompt request.
Find the metric practitioners already eyeball, instrument it, and ship the delta. A number turns a vibe into a product.
Put the model on the device and make connectivity a quality setting. It reads as a privacy feature and buys reliability for free.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A demo that needs the user to already know what to type. — then ComplianceGuardian made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any agent that touches production data

audit.worth_note: The product decision is the transferable one: refuse to let a model answer unless the answer names a rule from a versioned file, and escalate when it cannot. Pair that with an audit trail enforced at the permission layer and an entitlement model that spends counters inside a transaction, and you have three moves that apply to any agent product expected to produce evidence a third party will rely on. The incident write-up is unusually useful too - six failures behind each other, none of which crashed.

limits_disclosed.why: the team named what the system itself cannot do (cannot, fail)

numbers_add_up.why: 2 figure(s) a reader can check against the product (16 rulesets, 88 rules, 12 jurisdiction profiles; six defects stacked behind one another in the report pipeline), but 2 headline figure(s) carry no testable denominator: 536 passing tests; Stripe's INR conversion fee turned a $50 audit into 4,948 versus 4,200 rupees

stack_consistency.why: no repo to cross-check the declared stack against

test_or_eval_evidence.why: a harness is described (pytest) but no result, run link or case count is published, so it cannot be checked

assumptions: you pick one jurisdiction and one industry first, because 16 rulesets is a company not a hackathon
you have a GCP project you can run Cloud Tasks, BigQuery and Workflows against, and IAM rights to deny yourself
a domain reviewer is available; without one the rulesets are your own guess about the law
clone_cost.estimate: 2-3 weeks for the agent pair, gateway and append-only trail; months for defensible rulesets
clone_cost.why: The infrastructure they describe is standard GCP work and their two structural tricks are small to implement once you know them. What cannot be hurried is authoring and maintaining rule text for the jurisdictions you serve, plus someone qualified to confirm each rule still matches the regulation.

audit.what_to_steal: Grant the writer identity the append permission and deny it the job-starting permission, so history cannot be rewritten by the application that writes it; derive tenant identity only from verified token claims so there is no request field to tamper with; record prompt and model version against every generated verdict so a decision can be reproduced months later; make environment variables required rather than defaulted, because a permissive default on a fresh checkout silently removed credentials.
audit.what_breaks_first: The rulesets. Eighty-eight hand-authored YAML rules against regulations that amend without notice, with their own roadmap conceding that change detection is not built yet - so the first failure mode is a document auto-approved against a superseded rule, reported with a citation that still resolves to a real but obsolete clause. Second: the escalation threshold, since auto-approve on 'routine' documents is only as safe as the classifier that calls a document routine.

prior_art.relation: same audience, opposite instrument: that project signs an execution claim so a verifier can reject a mutation, this one cites a rule so a human can reject a reading. Read together they cover both halves of machine-checkable compliance - provenance and interpretation.

same shape (an agent pipeline that hands edge cases to a human) with a different optimisation target: Greenlight spends less, ComplianceGuardian refuses to be wrong quietly. The escalation path is the shared skeleton worth copying from either.

hazard.note: Compliance verdicts on NDIS, aged-care and privacy obligations, with routine documents auto-approved. The page argues its case for trustworthiness at length - citations, versioning, immutability - but does not state who is accountable when an auto-approved document later becomes an audit finding, nor whether the rulesets were reviewed by a practitioner.

newspectives-new-perspective-on-news.name: Newspectives - new perspective on news
newspectives-new-perspective-on-news.summary: One news event. Every regional lens. Side-by-side. Newspectives uses Google Gemini and Search grounding to compare how USA, China, Russia, Arab World and more frame each story - daily.

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: They built the thing that survives the no-budget, no-internet, no-permission case.
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: One news event. Every regional lens. Side-by-side. Newspectives uses Google Gemini and Search grounding to compare how USA, China, Russia, Arab World and more frame each story - daily.
steal_this: Steal the framing: Civics & Discourse work inside Public Trust, Safety & Compliance, done as a bounded loop.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A demo that needs the user to already know what to type. — then Newspectives - new perspective on news made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any agent that touches production data

audit.worth_note: The wedge is different in the way that matters for an agent-read catalog: it treats other models as first-class readers of a news product and builds for them - NewsArticle objects whose hasPart is an ItemList of Claim objects, one per perspective, each with its own anchor and citation array, a disambiguatingDescription marking the satirical lens so it is not quoted as fact, llms.txt, a 42,000-word llms-full.txt, ai-plugin.json, OpenAPI, IndexNow pings and an unauthenticated recent-topics endpoint. Almost nobody has taken that position, and for a product whose output will be summarized by machines it is the correct one: an agent should inherit the framing and the citations rather than a flattened paragraph. The editorial judgement is as sound as the plumbing - side by side rather than a merged balanced answer, Common Ground labelled as human curation, transparency pages at /methodology, /editorial-standards and /corrections. What holds it short of breakthrough is that the hard part is not built here: grounding quality, which the page itself names as the whole difference between perspective and ventriloquism, is unmeasured, and roughly ninety unresolved citation redirect URLs per topic page says the last mile of the citation layer is still open.

assumptions: grounding you can pin per region: search access to each region's press, plus a stated fallback label for when a region returns nothing
a citation pipeline that canonicalises publisher URLs, since redirect-chained citations are the part agents will inherit broken
editorial capacity for the synthesis and the corrections page, which the product presents as human curation and cannot automate without contradicting itself
a QA pass on what a lens may assert beyond its sources, before anyone treats the Claim objects as evidence rather than as framing
clone_cost.estimate: 6-9 weeks for the agent roster plus the schema surface; another quarter for the four media pipelines and the editorial tooling
clone_cost.why: The core loop is a fan-out with grounding: one event, N lens prompts each pinned to a region's outlets through search grounding, rendered side by side with tone labels - a few weeks in React, Express and Firestore, and the SPA-plus-Cloud-Run shape is well trodden. The work that is not routine is the surface the page treats as the product: emitting valid Claim-partitioned structured data per perspective with citation arrays, resolving grounded URLs to canonical publisher addresses (its own open defect), and keeping a public llms.txt, OpenAPI document and no-auth endpoint honest as the schema evolves. The radio bulletin, song and portrait video are each a separate third-party integration that fails silently often enough that the author wrote it up. And the editorial layer - curating Common Ground, maintaining /corrections - is recurring human cost rather than build cost, which is why a clone of this is smaller than its feature list and bigger than its line count.

audit.what_to_steal: Ship claim-level structured data rather than page-level: NewsArticle to hasPart to an ItemList of Claim objects, each perspective with its own @id anchor and citation array, so a consuming agent can attribute a sentence to a lens instead of to a URL. Use disambiguatingDescription to mark non-factual voices inside the same structure, and publish llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai-plugin.json, an OpenAPI document, IndexNow pings and an unauthenticated read endpoint - treat machine readers as an audience and the transparency pages become distribution. Then take the operational post-mortems, the most reusable content on the page: never return a 200 with a null payload (make it a real 502), bail after five consecutive nulls instead of polling an 'undefined' id fifty times, refuse to start on an empty or 'undefined' config value, treat silently ignored hosting config as untrustworthy and proxy it explicitly, dismiss splash screens in about 150ms and load auth and settings in the background, and remember that Admin SDK paths bypass security rules, so rule-only tests prove nothing about an admin UI. Last: keep synthesis human and say so on the page.
audit.what_breaks_first: The grounding fallback. When a region's outlets are unreachable - a paywall, a regional block, a story too new to have local coverage - the lens still produces fluent text, which is the exact failure the page names as ventriloquism, and there is no published policy for it and no rate for how often it happens. Second, citation integrity: about ninety redirect URLs per topic page still resolve through Vertex rather than to the publisher, so the citation array an agent inherits is a chain of third-party hops that can rot or 404 independently of the article. Third, the Jester: satire is marked with disambiguatingDescription, which most consumers ignore, so a joke line becomes a Claim in someone else's context window. Fourth, the Common Ground synthesis - labelled editorial curation on the site, but a downstream reader who takes the ItemList and drops the framing gets a machine-generated consensus view of a contested event, which is the one artifact this product's own principles say not to produce.

prior_art.relation: both convert an unverifiable judgement into a machine-checkable artifact - a signed finding in a CI matrix against a Claim object with a citation array - and both leave the same gap: the artifact proves the format, not the accuracy of what is inside it. ACM measures its own detectors while Newspectives does not measure its lenses, which is the sharper omission given that the lens output is read as fact by other models.

both attach citations to language a model generated and both keep a human as the writer of record, but they differ on direction and schedule: Continuity re-checks existing claims over time and hands back a diff, Newspectives generates fresh accounts of one event across regions and hands back a comparison. Neither publishes a false-negative rate, and in both cases that rate is what the user is actually buying.

both sit in the sector where the hazard question is sign-off and both answer it with transparency rather than authority - methodology, editorial-standards and corrections pages against an audit-ready rule set. The pair is the catalog's clearest illustration that disclosure and compliance are different objects: one tells a reader how the output was made, the other tells an auditor what was checked.
